overview: LiquidSense's Aura is a full-featured kill aura driven by the client event bus. Target selection runs from the pre-motion update, scoring every loaded entity by a configurable priority (Health, Distance, Direction, LivingTime) under FOV, hurt-time, range and team filters, then committing the first candidate whose rotations can be computed. The attack clock lives on Render3D, so clicks queue at the frame rate and are drained on the next update event, with the delay randomized between MinCPS and MaxCPS each cycle. Attacks leave as C02PacketUseEntity ATTACK behind an optional raycast hitable gate, and a six-mode autoblock subsystem (Vanilla, Pos, Both, Click, AAC, Interact) surrounds them with C08 block placements, keybind holds and C02 interacts. Silent rotations are the default, computed against the server rotation in RotationUtils and clamped by a randomized turn speed, with velocity prediction on the target bounding box and three rotation backends (Vanilla, BackTrack, Other).

sections.p: The module is split across five event handlers plus one packet interceptor. onMotion POST refreshes the hitable flag and starts blocking when the delayed-block switch is on, while the PRE phase calls update() which re-selects the target and binds currentTarget. onRender3D is the attack clock: when attackTimer has passed attackDelay and the target's hurtTime is at or below the HurtTime setting it increments the clicks counter and resets the timer with a fresh randomClickDelay between MinCPS and MaxCPS. onUpdate drains those clicks through runAttack() in a while loop, so the actual packet emission is decoupled from the render clock that schedules it. onStrafe rewrites strafe and forward inputs against the target rotation for the OldStrict, NewStrict and Silent strafe modes, and onEntityMove re-runs updateHitable whenever the tracked target changes its bounding box. onPacket intercepts C07PacketPlayerDigging only for the AAC autoblock mode, cancelling and re-queuing alternating release packets. A cancelRun guard (spectator, dead, Blink or FreeCam active) plus the NoInvAttack window freeze the whole pipeline, and the AAC mode also gates on the inventory screen state.

updateTarget scans mc.theWorld.loadedEntityList and applies isEnemy, which composes the global EntityUtils filters with LiquidSense's own AntiBot, NoHurt, Teams and NoFriends checks, then keeps entities whose box distance is within maxRange (the larger of Range and BlockRange), whose rotation difference is within FOV, and whose hurtTime is at or below the threshold. The survivors are sorted by the Priority setting and each candidate is passed to updateRotations, which must succeed for the entity to become the target; when every candidate fails, prevTargetEntities is cleared and the scan retries. The Vanilla backend calls RotationUtils.searchCenter on the entity bounding box, optionally offset by the entity velocity times a random factor in [MinPredictSize, MaxPredictSize] when Predict is on, with random-center and outborder sampling; BackTrack uses RotationUtils.OtherRotation the same way; Other uses OtherRotationUtils.searchCenter and latches a Rotationhit boolean when the limited rotation lands within 5 degrees. Every backend funnels through limitAngleChange against serverRotation with a random per-tick cap between MinTurnSpeed and MaxTurnSpeed, and the result is applied either silently through setTargetRotation (with a 15ms lag when the AAC switch is on) or visibly by writing the angles into the player.

runAttack checks the hitable flag, which is set by a RaycastUtils.raycastEntity sweep at reach = min(maxRange, box distance) + 1.4 when RayCast is on or by RotationUtils.isFaced otherwise, and randomly skips the hit when FailRate rolls, emitting only a swing when FakeSwing is enabled. A real hit sends swingItem plus C02PacketUseEntity ATTACK; the KeepSprint path plays the critical and enchantment particles locally, while the vanilla path calls attackTargetEntityWithCurrentItem. Multi mode iterates every enemy within range and attacks them in one pass, stopping at LimitedMultiTargets when set. The autoblock modes differ only in how the block state is asserted: Vanilla sends C08 with the held item, Pos sends C08 against BlockPos(-1,-1,-1) with facing 255, Both sends two C08 packets, Click holds the use-item key binding, and AAC toggles the binding and relies on the C07 cancellation flip. InteractAutoBlock additionally sends a C02 INTERACT with the entity position vector before blocking. The AAC mode also closes and re-opens the inventory around each attack (C0D close, C16 open) to mask the cooldown reset, and FakeSharp forces the enchantment critical effect even without a sharpness enchant.

files.label: Aura.kt (module logic)
files.explanation: The entire module lives in this one Kotlin file: the value declarations that define the CPS window, range, FOV, priority, target mode and rotation mode switches, the five event handlers that schedule and drain attacks, the target-selection and isEnemy filters, the three rotation backends, and every autoblock mode including the AAC inventory trick. updateTarget and updateRotations are the two methods that decide what gets attacked and from which angle, and runAttack is the single place where C02PacketUseEntity leaves the client. The onPacket handler is the only code path that touches outgoing C07 packets, and it exists purely to service the AAC autoblock mode's cancellation flip. Reading the file from the value block at the top gives the full configurable surface, while the event handlers at the bottom show the render-clock scheduling that ties attack rate to frame rate.

files.label: RotationUtils.java (rotation math and silent application)
files.explanation: RotationUtils implements everything the Aura needs to aim: searchCenter picks a point inside the target bounding box (with outborder and random-center sampling), OtherRotation computes the alternative backtracking angle, limitAngleChange clamps a rotation to a maximum per-tick delta against the stored serverRotation, and setTargetRotation feeds the silent-rotation pipeline that rewrites the player's yaw and pitch in outgoing movement packets without moving the visual camera. getRotationDifference scores how far an entity sits from the current look direction and powers both the FOV filter and the Direction priority sort. isFaced is the fallback hitable test used when the RayCast switch is off. The class is shared with the client's other combat modules, but the Aura is the heaviest consumer: every attack cycle calls searchCenter or OtherRotation, limits the result, and applies it, which is exactly the rotation stream an aim-pattern check would analyze.

countering.label: AimbotHeuristic (rotation pattern analysis)
countering.explanation: Hawk's AimbotHeuristic records every look delta as a Vector(yawChange, pitchChange) in a per-player list and walks the recent history scoring speed and the angle between consecutive moves. It fires on three signatures: all recent moves sharing one speed and direction (maxSpeed - minSpeed > 4 with minSpeed below 0.01, maxAngle below 0.1 and a preceding move faster than 1), a pair of consecutive high-speed rotations with a sharp turn between them (speed and lastSpeed both over 20 with angle over 2.86), and a sudden deceleration of more than 30 with an angle over 0.8. These are the exact shapes a scripted snap leaves in the yaw/pitch stream, and because Hawk reads the rotations that actually reach the server, silent rotation does not hide them.

countering.label: KillAura (direction, multi, reach, speed)
countering.explanation: Arc's KillAura check runs from the FightListener on every attack and combines four independent sub-checks. The direction check computes the angle between the player's look vector and the attacked entity and flags anything above max-direction-angle; the multi sub-check compares the angles to the last and current attacked entity and flags when they differ by more than maxAngle while both are in reach; the reach sub-check measures the distance from the player to the entity position minus its velocity, so knockback does not mask an out-of-range hit; and the speed sub-check counts attacks and attack packets per second against max-attacks and max-attack-packets, resetting on a one-second boundary. The no-swing sub-check is also present but fires only when an attack arrives without an arm swing inside max-swing-time.

countering.label: Reach (distance limit with precision and dynamic reduction)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight.Reach validates every attack against a server-side distance limit. check() computes the player-to-entity distance lenpRel, picks distanceLimit from reachSurvivalDistance (with a separate 6.5 limit in creative), and flags when lenpRel exceeds the limit, optionally tightened by reachPrecision which compares the actual separation instead of the relaxed box margin. Repeated violations accumulate reachVL and drive a dynamic reduction: reachReduceDistance shrinks the effective limit step by step, and when the module cancels, reachPenalty applies an attack penalty that further suppresses the player's combat ability. The comparison runs on the server's own positions, so nothing the client claims about range or facing changes the measured distance.
